BioNTech halts mid-stage trial of personalized mRNA vaccine in colorectal cancer
snippet: Shares of Germany-based BioNTech were down as much as 8% Friday after announcing a Phase 2 trial of autogene cevumeran would be discontinued for futility. The news follows Merck and Moderna’s Phase 3 win last week for their cancer vaccine plus Keytruda in melanoma.

title: ‘Worse than expected’ Wainua data muddies water for TTR silencers
snippet: AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ data drop divulging more details from its highly watched Phase 3 transthyretin silencer trial “further confuses the picture” for Wainua when combined with the standard of care for ATTR-CM, analysts say.

title: BioXcel files for bankruptcy, will sell assets to Teva for up to $125M
snippet: Teva Pharmaceuticals is the 'stalking horse bidder' to kick off the auction process for BioXcel Therapeutics' AI-derived assets as the biotech files for Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

title: Lilly joins Novo in cardiovascular space after FDA nod for GLP-1/GIP agonist Mounjaro
snippet: With the approval, Eli Lilly’s Mounjaro becomes the first dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist indicated to lower the risk of heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death in adults with type 2 diabetes.

title: Genentech strikes second Asia deal in a week, betting up to $1B in oncology ADC alliance with DualityBio
snippet: Through its DualityBio deal, Roche's Genentech hopes to create antibody-drug conjugates with payloads that can circumvent growing cancer drug resistance.

title: Priovant nabs first FDA approval for targeted tablet in dermatomyositis
snippet: Lisraya carries a boxed warning typical of JAK inhibitors, but otherwise has a broad label that allows use in all adults with the rare autoimmune disease, setting up the drug for blockbuster status in a few years, according to Leerink.

title: AstraZeneca, Amgen poised to challenge Dupixent’s reign with esophagitis win
snippet: Even without specific Phase 3 data yet revealed, analysts see AstraZeneca and Amgen’s Tezspire as a potential threat for Dupixent in eosinophilic esophagitis.

title: Multispecifics are transforming the CDMO development architecture
snippet: Manufacturers are being pushed beyond mAb‑era platforms into a new design model built around molecular engineering, complex analytics and amplified upstream and downstream processing.

title: CAR T for autoimmune disease benefits from oncology’s lessons—and will deliver its own
snippet: Thanks in part to the revolution cell therapy brought to treating blood cancers, the modality is now showing promise in some autoimmune applications. This expansion is poised to yield even wider benefits.

title: Generate Bio drops as data accidentally leaked ahead of European conference
snippet: Phase 1 data from Generate Biomedicines’ ongoing chronic obstructive pulmonary disease study demonstrated “rapid and sustained reductions” across four disease biomarkers.

title: RevMed could become ‘next oncology titan’ with Rasonque nod
snippet: A future expansion of Rasonque into first-line pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma could set Revolution Medicines up to hit $2.3 billion in sales by 2028, according to Truist Securities.

title: AstraZeneca, Amgen notch another late-stage win for Tezspire, this time in esophagitis
snippet: AstraZeneca and Amgen co-develop and co-commercialize Tezspire under an April 2012 agreement. The partners are now planning another FDA submission for the asthma drug, which received an expansion into chronic rhinosinusitis last year.

From trial endpoints and placebo effects to neuroplasticity modulation, we explore what it will take to build a sustainable path to the f...

title: Nearly 1/4 dealing with long-term unemployment call it quits on biopharma job searches
snippet: Limited opportunities and burnout are just two reasons biopharma professionals stop looking for work, with some pivoting away from the industry or turning to consulting. Two career coaches discuss why ending a job hunt is harmful and what to do instead.

title: The great disconnect: 4 ways companies, job candidates misalign
snippet: Two recruiting experts discuss the main areas where biopharma employers and candidates don’t match up, from how the hiring process runs to what companies can truly pay new employees.

title: CAR Ts will only treat autoimmune diseases if we can scale delivery
snippet: Biopharmas developing CAR T therapies for autoimmune indications face major barriers to maximizing the market. Advances in the provider ecosystem and clinical infrastructure, as well as access and education, will be key to launching at scale.

title: Myriad catalysts on deck for obesity’s brightest stars as market continues to accelerate
snippet: Current leaders Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk have cornered the early market for weight loss therapeutics, but several other players, large and small, are bidding for a piece of the potential $200 billion pie.

title: Vitruvias vanishes amid thyroid tablets recall over potential ‘superpotency’ concerns
snippet: Vitruvias Therapeutics has “ceased operations” after voluntarily recalling a batch recall of generic thyroid tablets due to possible superpotency that could cause a range of adverse events.

title: RevMed receives early FDA approval for ‘groundbreaking’ pancreatic cancer drug
snippet: The FDA granted the approval of Revolution Medicines' daraxonrasib, now to be known as Rasonque, in pancreatic adenocarcinoma 6.5 months ahead of deadline.

title: Summit, Akeso tout biliary cancer win for PD-1/VEGF in China—but details are pending
snippet: The Phase 3 readout is the first for ivonescimab beyond non-small cell lung cancer to show a significant overall survival benefit, according to Summit Therapeutics and China-based partner Akeso.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
